sources.name: NASA Science, Our Sun: Facts (spectral type G2 V)
sources.note: SIMBAD does not catalogue the Sun, so its spectral type is taken from NASA.

notes: Planet positions use JPL low-accuracy Keplerian elements; they are not a high-precision ephemeris. The table in `validation` records the error against JPL Horizons.
Satellite positions use osculating elements at the reference epoch with JPL mean periods; accuracy degrades with distance in time from the epoch.
Body orientation uses the linear terms of the IAU elements only.
The Sun is placed at the origin; its motion about the barycentre is ignored.

facts.text: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star (spectral type G2V). It rotates differentially: its equator turns faster than its poles, so the single rotation period given is an adopted value.
facts.reference: NASA Science (spectral type G2 V); JPL Horizons adopted sidereal period

facts.text: Its luminosity and effective temperature are the IAU 2015 nominal values; the Sun’s actual output varies slightly over the 11-year activity cycle.

facts.text: Mercury has no substantial atmosphere, only a thin surface-bounded exosphere, so its surface temperature swings by hundreds of kelvin between day and night.
Radar and MESSENGER data indicate water ice in permanently shadowed craters near the poles. The ice is inferred from reflectance, radar and neutron data rather than sampled directly.

facts.text: Its surface is permanently hidden by opaque sulfuric-acid cloud, so visible-light images show an almost featureless disc. The surface has been mapped only by radar (Magellan) and a few landers.

facts.text: About 71% of Earth’s surface is covered by liquid-water oceans (JPL lists 3.62×10⁸ km² of sea and 1.48×10⁸ km² of land).
Earth is the only place known to host life. Its Moon raises the ocean tides.

facts.text: The Moon rotates synchronously, so the same hemisphere always faces Earth.
The leading hypothesis is that the Moon formed from debris of a giant impact between the early Earth and a Mars-sized body. It is widely supported but not directly confirmed.
facts.reference: NASA lunar science (Apollo sample and LRO results)

facts.text: Europa has a young, fractured water-ice surface with few impact craters.

Several lines of evidence, including Galileo magnetometer data showing an induced magnetic field, indicate a global liquid-water ocean beneath the ice shell. The ocean has not been observed directly, so this is a strong inference rather than a confirmed observation. NASA’s Europa Clipper mission, launched in 2024, is designed to investigate it.
facts.reference: NASA Galileo results; Europa Clipper mission

facts.text: Whether Europa’s ocean could support life is an open question.

facts.text: Triton orbits Neptune retrograde (its orbital inclination, as listed by JPL, is above 90 degrees).
Triton is thought to be a captured Kuiper-belt object because of that retrograde orbit. This is the leading hypothesis, not a confirmed fact.
Voyager 2 imaged dark plumes rising from Triton’s surface, evidence of current geysers.
